correctness.rationale: The fully specified Gaussian sampling operator is unitarily conjugate to the derived two-by-two Fourier multiplier. Parity autocorrelation gives exact determinant -D theta4 and norm squared 2 A theta3, and Poisson/Jacobi product methods show all required positivity and strict monotonicity. Uniform even-order singular perturbation yields the fourth-order error; analytic modular asymptotics yield both extreme-width laws. The Hermite symbol is boundedly invertible on the entire frequency circle. Independent direct numeric matrix checks (3033 assertions) support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Near-coincident point-sampling is a natural stability boundary of the published critical-density Gaussian interpolation problem. The theorem identifies an unknown continuum-optimal theta-function coefficient, its unique worst quasi-frequency, an exact regularization through Hermite observations at critical density, and two substantially different sharp Gaussian-width regimes. These yield nontrivial structural and quantitative information rather than a routine normalization check; no extension to arbitrary nonperiodic arrays is claimed.
